answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut mandate combined with incumbent refusal to reopen pricing creates a hard constraint that negotiation alone cannot solve (memory_c4 shows negotiation recovered margin but the incumbent has already refused this cycle). Renewing at current terms violates the financial mandate. Deferring is impossible given the 14-day deadline and no auto-renewal. Adding a second source without solving primary cost leaves the base spend unaddressed. Memory_c2 demonstrates that switching to a low-cost vendor can cut unit cost sharply with fast onboarding and reliable invoicing—this is the only path that achieves the 18% reduction target. The 94% line utilization creates delivery risk, but memory_c2 explicitly shows accurate invoicing and quick onboarding mitigates transition risk. A standard experiment approach (phased volume transfer rather than immediate full cutover) preserves some incumbent relationship as fallback if the new vendor underperforms on delivery. This flags downstream risk because losing the incumbent relationship removes a known-stable integration pattern (memory_c1), but the financial mandate leaves no operational alternative.
